The Machine Learning internship in short

In the SkillMe Machine Learning internship you build one of 3 projects, such as VisionAI: Local Computer Vision & Multi-Modal Intelligence Studio, a project where you teach a computer to recognise handwritten digits, starting with scikit-learn and finishing with a draw-a-digit web app. In week 1 you load a small dataset of handwritten digit images, look at them, and train your first classifier with scikit-learn. By week 4 you train a small convolutional neural network (CNN) with Keras, compare it with your scikit-learn model, and let users pick either model in your app. Each milestone is posted on LinkedIn and checked against that week's checklist before it counts. Top performers earn a stipend of up to $100 a month.

Week by week

What each week of the Machine Learning internship covers

Shown for VisionAI: Local Computer Vision & Multi-Modal Intelligence Studio. The other projects follow the same four-week shape.

  1. Week 1 of 4

    Your First Image Classifier with scikit-learn

    Beginner2-3 hours

    You will load a small dataset of handwritten digit images, look at them, and train your first classifier with scikit-learn. This teaches the core machine learning loop you will reuse all month: load data, split it, train, and measure on data the model has never seen.

    What you learn

    • How images are stored as grids of pixel numbers
    • Features (X) and labels (y) in supervised learning
    • Why we split data into training and test sets
    • Training and scoring a K-Nearest Neighbours classifier

    What you submit

    • A notebook (week1_digits.ipynb) that runs top to bottom without errors
    • A grid of sample digit images with their labels
    • A table of test accuracy for different n_neighbors values
    • A prediction grid showing predicted vs actual labels on test images
    How week 1 is reviewed
    • The notebook runs from a fresh kernel with no errors
    • The model is trained only on the training split and scored on the test split
    • Test accuracy is printed and is above 90%
    • At least 4 values of n_neighbors are compared in a table
    • The README states the dataset, the model and the best test accuracy

    Stretch goal: Train a LogisticRegression model on the same split and see whether it beats your best KNN score.

  2. Week 2 of 4

    Compare Models and Learn from Mistakes

    Beginner+2-3 hours

    You will compare several classifiers fairly, find out which digits your model confuses, and move up to the full-size MNIST dataset. Knowing how to evaluate a model honestly matters more than any single algorithm.

    What you learn

    • Comparing models fairly with cross-validation
    • Reading a confusion matrix to see which classes get mixed up
    • Why feature scaling helps some models
    • Saving a trained model to a file with joblib

    What you submit

    • A bar chart comparing cross-validation scores of at least 4 models
    • A confusion matrix and a gallery of misclassified images
    • A trained MNIST model saved as digit_model.joblib
    • A results section in the README explaining which model won and why
    How week 2 is reviewed
    • At least 4 models are compared using 5-fold cross-validation on the training data
    • The test set is used only once, for the final chosen model
    • The confusion matrix is shown and the README names the two digits most often confused
    • The MNIST model reaches at least 93% test accuracy
    • digit_model.joblib loads in a fresh notebook and makes predictions

    Stretch goal: Use GridSearchCV to tune two hyperparameters of your best model and report whether the score improved.

  3. Week 3 of 4

    Draw-a-Digit Web App with Gradio

    Intermediate2-3 hours

    You will wrap your saved MNIST model in a Gradio web app where anyone can draw or upload a digit and see the prediction. Real users send messy input, so this week is about preparing images correctly and handling errors gracefully.

    What you learn

    • Turning a real image into the exact format the model was trained on
    • Building a simple web interface with Gradio
    • Showing prediction confidence with predict_proba
    • Handling bad input without crashing the app

    What you submit

    • A Gradio app (app.py) that runs locally with python app.py
    • Sketchpad and upload inputs that show the top-3 predictions with confidence
    • Friendly error messages for empty or invalid input
    • A requirements.txt and a README with run instructions and your real-world accuracy
    How week 3 is reviewed
    • The app starts with python app.py after installing from requirements.txt
    • Drawing a digit shows the top-3 predictions with probabilities
    • An empty canvas and an invalid file each show a message instead of a crash
    • The model is loaded once, not on every prediction
    • The README reports your real-world accuracy on 20 hand-drawn digits

    Stretch goal: Crop and centre the drawn digit before resizing (as MNIST does) and measure whether your real-world accuracy improves.

  4. Week 4 of 4

    Capstone: Add a Neural Network and Ship It

    Intermediate+2-3 hours

    You will train a small convolutional neural network (CNN) with Keras, compare it with your scikit-learn model, and let users pick either model in your app. You finish with a polished README and a demo video that tells the story of your project.

    What you learn

    • What layers, epochs and loss mean in a neural network
    • How a small CNN learns patterns from images
    • Plotting training vs validation accuracy to spot overfitting
    • Presenting a project clearly with a README and demo

    What you submit

    • A CNN training notebook with an accuracy-per-epoch plot
    • An updated Gradio app with a model switcher
    • A results table comparing both models on the test set and on your own drawings
    • A final README and a 60-second demo video
    How week 4 is reviewed
    • The CNN reaches at least 97% test accuracy
    • The app lets a user switch models and both return predictions
    • The results table shows test accuracy and real-world accuracy for both models
    • A new person can install and run the app by following the README
    • The demo video is under 90 seconds and shows the app working live

    Stretch goal: Add a Fashion-MNIST mode that classifies clothing images using the same app structure.

Is it for you?

Who the Machine Learning internship is for, and what you leave with

This internship fits you if

  • You know the basics of PyTorch, Scikit-Learn and Pandas and want a real project to show for it, not more tutorials.
  • You can start at beginner level. Week 1: You will load a small dataset of handwritten digit images, look at them, and train your first classifier with scikit-learn.
  • You want to reach intermediate+ level in four weeks. Week 4: You will train a small convolutional neural network (CNN) with Keras, compare it with your scikit-learn model, and let users pick either model in your app.
  • You can give it about 2-3 hours a week around college or a job, from any country.

Machine Learning internship: questions and answers

What will I build in the Machine Learning internship?

You are assigned one of 3 projects: VisionAI: Local Computer Vision & Multi-Modal Intelligence Studio, NeuroNLP: Semantic Text Intelligence & Sentiment Studio or PriceWise: House Price Prediction App. Each is a single project built up over four weekly milestones, so each week adds to the last.

What skills will I learn in the Machine Learning internship?

The Machine Learning internship works with PyTorch, Scikit-Learn and Pandas. Week 1: how images are stored as grids of pixel numbers; features (X) and labels (y) in supervised learning. Week 2: comparing models fairly with cross-validation; reading a confusion matrix to see which classes get mixed up. Week 3: turning a real image into the exact format the model was trained on; building a simple web interface with Gradio. Week 4: what layers, epochs and loss mean in a neural network; how a small CNN learns patterns from images.

Do I need experience to apply for the Machine Learning internship?

You need the basics of PyTorch, Scikit-Learn and Pandas, not prior internship experience. Week 1 starts at beginner level, where you load a small dataset of handwritten digit images, look at them, and train your first classifier with scikit-learn. Week 4 reaches intermediate+ level. A short screening quiz (8 questions, about 5 minutes) checks you are ready to start.

How is each Machine Learning milestone reviewed?

Every week has a checklist, and a milestone is approved only when it meets all of it. For week 1 of VisionAI: Local Computer Vision & Multi-Modal Intelligence Studio, that means: the notebook runs from a fresh kernel with no errors; the model is trained only on the training split and scored on the test split; test accuracy is printed and is above 90%; at least 4 values of n_neighbors are compared in a table; the README states the dataset, the model and the best test accuracy. Reviewers include engineers who work at Walmart, Google and LinkedIn, and work that misses the bar comes back with notes.

What can I put on my resume after the Machine Learning internship?

Each approved milestone gives you a line you can back up with a public LinkedIn post: Built my first image classifier in Python using scikit-learn's handwritten digits dataset; Trained a K-Nearest Neighbours model that scored over 90% accuracy on a held-out test set; Visualised the model's predictions and compared results for different values of k; Compared four scikit-learn classifiers fairly using 5-fold cross-validation; Used a confusion matrix and a gallery of mistakes to understand where my model fails; Scaled my digit classifier up to the full 28x28 MNIST dataset and saved it for reuse; Built a draw-a-digit web app with Gradio that predicts handwritten digits live; Wrote an image preprocessing step that converts real drawings into MNIST format; Added confidence scores and error handling, and measured accuracy on my own drawings; Trained a convolutional neural network with Keras that reached over 97% accuracy on MNIST; Compared a deep learning model with a classic scikit-learn model on test data and real drawings; Shipped a draw-a-digit Gradio app with a model switcher and a clear README.

What are the other projects in the Machine Learning internship?

NeuroNLP: Semantic Text Intelligence & Sentiment Studio: Build a tool that reads movie or product reviews and tells you whether they are positive or negative. PriceWise: House Price Prediction App: Predict house prices from simple features and let users explore 'what if' questions in a web app. Every project follows the same four-week shape, with one reviewed milestone a week.

Is the Machine Learning internship paid? Is there a stipend?

Top performers earn a stipend of up to $100 a month. It is performance-based and goes to the interns whose reviewed Machine Learning work stands out in their cohort, not to every intern.

How much time does it take?

4 weeks, one milestone a week, each planned for about 2-3 hours. It is fully remote and open worldwide, so you work around college or a job.
